#| include: false

knitr::opts_chunk$set(

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tinytable)
library(ggplot2)
library(kfbmisc)

# http://www.color-hex.com/color-palette/1146
skittles_palette <- c(
  "Red" = "#c0043f",
  "Orange" = "#e64808",
  "Yellow" = "#f1be02",
  "Green" = "#048207",
  "Purple" = "#441349"
)

skittles <- bind_rows(
  read.csv("data/skittles_data_F2026.csv"),
  read.csv("data/skittles_data_reddit.csv")
)
skittles$Total <- skittles$Red +
  skittles$Orange +
  skittles$Yellow +
  skittles$Green +
  skittles$Purple

skittles_long <- skittles |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c("Red", "Orange", "Yellow", "Green", "Purple"),
    names_to = "color",
    values_to = "count"
  ) |>
  select(Pack, color, count, Total) |>
  mutate(
    share = count / Total
  )

draws_long <- skittles |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(First_Draw, Second_Draw, Third_Draw, Fourth_Draw),
    names_to = "draw",
    values_to = "color"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    draw_number = match(
      draw,
      c("First_Draw", "Second_Draw", "Third_Draw", "Fourth_Draw")
    )
  )
```

## Raw Data {.unnumbered}

Each bar represents one pack, with the colored sections showing how many
Skittles of each color it contains. This plot shows the variation from pack to
pack and makes it possible to compare the total counts and color composition
of individual packs. Are the packs similar in their color composition, or are
some colors noticeably more common in particular packs? The plot also gives us
a first look at whether the packs appear to contain a consistent number of
Skittles.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Color Counts by Pack"
ggplot() +
  geom_bar(
    aes(x = Pack, y = count, fill = color),
    data = skittles_long,
    stat = "identity"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(1, 36, by = 3),
    minor_breaks = NULL,
    expand = expansion(0, 0.2)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = skittles_palette) +
  labs(
    x = "Pack Number",
    y = "Skittle Count",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_kyle(legend = "top") +
  kfbmisc::barchart_settings()
``` 


## Number of Skittles per Pack {.unnumbered}

The average number of Skittles per pack is `r sprintf("%0.2f", mean(skittles$Total, na.rm = TRUE))` with a standard deviation of `r sprintf("%0.2f", sd(skittles$Total, na.rm = TRUE))`. Is this
variation small enough to describe the packs as consistent, or do pack totals
differ substantially?
The histogram shows how the total number of Skittles is distributed across the
packs collected by the class. The solid curve is the smoothed density of the
observed totals, while the dashed curve is a normal distribution with the same
mean and standard deviation.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Total Number Skittles in a Pack"
ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(x = Total, y = after_stat(count) / sum(after_stat(count))),
    data = skittles,
    fill = "grey50",
    binwidth = 1,
    alpha = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_density(
    aes(x = Total, color = "Density Curve"),
    data = skittles,
    linewidth = 1.5,
    key_glyph = "path"
  ) +
  ## Normal approximation
  stat_function(
    aes(color = "Normal Distribution"),
    fun = function(x) {
      dnorm(x, mean = mean(skittles$Total), sd = sd(skittles$Total))
    },
    xlim = range(skittles$Total),
    # color = "grey50",
    linewidth = 1.5,
    linetype = "dashed",
    key_glyph = "path"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("grey50", kyle_color("magenta")),
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Number of Skittles in Pack",
    y = "Share of Packs with this Count",
    fill = NULL,
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_kyle(legend = "top") +
  kfbmisc::barchart_settings()
```


## Color Proportions in Early Draws {.unnumbered}

This figure compares the color proportions observed after the first one, two,
three, and four draws. Comparing the groups shows how the observed mix changes
as more Skittles are included in the sample. With only a few draws, how much
can the observed color mix vary just by chance? Does the mix become more
representative of the available colors as the number of draws increases?

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Color Proportions in the First Three Draws"
draw_proportions <- draws_long |>
  crossing(draws_included = 1:4) |>
  filter(draw_number <= draws_included) |>
  count(draws_included, color) |>
  complete(
    draws_included,
    color = names(skittles_palette),
    fill = list(n = 0)
  ) |>
  group_by(draws_included) |>
  mutate(
    proportion = n / sum(n),
    draws = factor(
      draws_included,
      levels = 1:4,
      labels = c(
        "First draw",
        "First two draws",
        "First three draws",
        "First four draws"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(draw_proportions, aes(x = draws, y = proportion, fill = color)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = skittles_palette) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Proportion of Draws",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_kyle(legend = "top") +
  kfbmisc::barchart_settings()
```



## Distribution of Each Color {.unnumbered}

The five panels show the distribution of each color's share within a pack.
The horizontal position of a pack depends on the proportion of its Skittles
that have that color, so the panels can be compared for center and spread. The
dashed vertical line at 20% marks the expected share when all five colors are
equally common. Is the average share of each color close to 20%? Which colors
are most consistent from pack to pack, and which show the greatest variation?

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Distribution across Repeated Sampling"
ggplot() +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0.2,
    linewidth = 0.75,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey70"
  ) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(x = share, fill = color, color = color),
    data = skittles_long,
    binwidth = 0.01,
    alpha = 0.4
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~color) +
  labs(
    x = "Proportion of Skittles of this Color in a Pack",
    y = "Number of Packs",
    fill = NULL,
    color = NULL
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = skittles_palette, guide = guide_none()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = skittles_palette, guide = guide_none()) +
  theme_kyle(legend = "top", grid_minor = "v") +
  kfbmisc::barchart_settings()
```


What is the average share of each color per pack?

```{r}
skittles_long |>
  summarize(.by = color, mean_share = mean(share), sd_share = sd(share)) |>
  setNames(c(
    "Color",
    "Average Proportion in Pack",
    "Std. Dev. of Proportion across Packs"
  )) |>
  tt(caption = "Summary of Sample Distribution") |>
  format_tt(j = c(2, 3), fn = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.02))
```
